abstract: Following the publication of the government's UK Cyber Security Strategy in November 2011, Louise Bennett FBCS CITP gives her thoughts on it and what it means for the industry and the nation.

Practically all commercial businesses rely on passive cyber defence. A company's information assurance strategy is dependent on a combination of software, business processes and human resources - of these the most important is continuous education of the human resources says John Curry MBCS.

Matthew Swindells, Chair, BCS Health, recently spoke to the Primary Health Care Specialist Group (PHCSG) on using IT to improve population health management. This article is a summary of what he talked about.

The NHS Future Forum, Chaired by GP Professor Steve Field, has recommended that patients should be given the right to access their medical records online. Matthew Swindells, Chair of BCS Health, considers how health informatics professionals should respond to this initiative.

Anil Hansjee MBCS CITP is Chair of the newly formed Entrepreneurs Specialist Group. He has previously worked at Google, where he ran mergers and acquisitions. He started out as a software engineer but has also worked as a venture capitalist in the IT entrepreneurial scene, in investment banking and more recently as an angel investor for start-ups. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about the new group.

articleTitle: SFIA at the Heart of Business Change
abstract: IBM Certified Consulting Learning Specialist Paul Jagger FBCS explains how SFIA version 5 repositions learning and development (L&D) at the heart of business change.

Following the launch of the BCS Entrepreneur Specialist Group, BCS held an event to discuss whether entrepreneurship is something you can do as a career. There were six speakers and a question and answer discussion followed. Henry Tucker MBCS reports.
Just when you thought it was safe to get your phone out, it seems there is yet more cell (phone) craziness out there according to phone botherer Henry Tucker MBCS.

Following on from his plenary speech at this year's BCS health conference, HC2012, Justin Richards, Multimedia Editor, BCS, spoke to Earl Howe, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Health, about the importance of IT to healthcare and his thoughts on the current reforms.
The winners of the UK IT industry awards were announced at a glamorous ceremony on 14 November.

articleTitle: Health Informatics a Frontline Activity Everyone Needs to Understand
abstract: Ensuring the safety of everyone who comes into contact with health services is one of the most important challenges facing healthcare organisations today. Dr Jean Roberts CEng FBCS CITP, Director (Standards) for the UK Council for Health Informatics Professions, discusses the issues.
Jooli Atkins, Chair of the Learning and Development SG and regular BCS blogger, gives her view on businesses' perception of whether or not IT professionals need a ‘softer’ side.

Like most security professionals, Michele Daryanani is vociferous when it comes to the role that user education plays in IT security. If we bombard users with security warning messages, surely that should aid in educating users – even if they only read a handful of the messages, right? Or is less really more in this case?

With global smartphone usage at almost 50 per cent, there are many apps available that can be used to monitor your health, keep you fit or give useful advice. Henry Tucker MBCS downloaded some apps to see how good they are.

Mark Dorling is a teacher and the Digital Schoolhouse co-ordinator at Langley Grammar school. He spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about the project and why it is important to teach computer science to children.
China is the word's first cyber superpower and has the means to perform cyber warfare according to Lt Colonel Hagestad II and Tim Price.
How do we make security easier and security status more visible? Peter Bagnall, a software architect and interaction designer, has a few ideas.

Tyrone Edward FBCS is Director in the Forensic Technology and Discovery Services Group at Ernst and Young, which is in the Fraud Investigation and Disputes practice at Ernst and Young. Brian Runciman MBCS spoke to him about his role.

Over the last two or so years, organisations have had to meet a new and highly specific online threat. That threat is hacktivism and Adrian Davis, Principal Research Analyst at the Information Security Forum, takes a look at the threat from an information security perspective, based on research conducted by the Information Security Forum and the experiences of its 300 global member organisations.

Reporters can now tweet and email in England and Wales to communicate court proceedings live. They no longer have to seek the court's consent case-by-case, as they did for the extradition proceedings for Julian Assange, Wikileaks' founder, over a year ago, says IT lawyer and past President Rachel Burnett.
John Mitchell has not yet been defrauded or attacked by a computer of its own volition. There has always been some guiding human influence.

In the first of a series of reports on BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT's health conference, HC2012, Matthew Swindells, Chair BCS Health, kicks things off with a personal highlight from this year's conference, namely of his announcement of BCS Healthapos;s partnership with the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS).
At the judging day for the 2012 BCS UK IT Industry Awards, Henry Tucker MBCS spoke to some of the finalists in the business IT innovation category about their projects.
John Mitchell's job makes him cynical and is the reason he trusts few people.
BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, has signed an agreement with the International Software Quality Institute (iSQI GmbH) to be an exam provider for the Certified Agile Tester certificate.

It's March already and the dark economic clouds are still gathered over Europe. With each passing week we all search for signs of the green shoots of economic recovery says John Brazier, PCG Managing Director.

With unemployment in the UK at its highest in decades and over one million 16-24 year olds out of work, young, as well as many experienced, professionals are stopping at nothing to find work. Many job seekers are now turning to Facebook as a new way in. Juan Urdiales, jobandtalent Co-founder and Co-CEO, reports.
Criminals are going to ever more extreme lengths to get access to company systems and home computers, according to Les Ball and Natalie Coull.

articleTitle: Left of the Inside Back Cover

abstract: Five years ago everyone was talking about virtual worlds, such as Second Life, and how they could be used in business. Henry Tucker MBCS asks if they are still there.
On a visit to New York, John Mitchell had an encounter with a rather well-informed janitor, proving you can't always know who you're talking to or dealing with.
It has been a long time since I have seen a new development in IT divide opinions in the way that cloud has done, says Chris Tiernan FBCS CITP, as he reports on a recent BCS Elite Group event.
Richard Hodkinson CEng CITP gives you a flavour of the challenges of working in IT in the legal area.

Gartner has been conducting a global CIO survey for more than 10 years. 2012's CIO survey contains results from 2335 CIOs around the world, including 850 from EMEA, 170 from the UK. This year's results reveal a complex mix of macroeconomic uncertainty and technology opportunity, says David Aron a Vice President and Research Fellow at Gartner.

The Institute publishes new reports from analyst Forrester every month. Members have access to the full text, this is an overview of recent reports.

IT will feature in almost every aspect of the forthcoming Olympic Games in London, including helping keep athletes and spectators safe. Henry Tucker MBCS spoke to Steve Whatson, Director of ICT for the Olympics at Metropolitan Police Service, about the IT systems in place for the emergency services.

articleTitle: How to reduce the cost of software testing

abstract: Below are based on extracts from the British Computer Society's eminent academic monthly, The Computer Journal, published with Oxford University Press.
The Institute publishes new reports from analyst Forrester every month. Members have access to the full text, this is an overview of recent reports.
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, takes a glimpse into the future * to see what emerging threats we might have to contend with.
Have you considered a career in security? Mike Westmacott MBCS CITP says the time is right.
Brian Runciman MBCS spoke to Martyn Ware, founder of The Human League and Heaven 17, about his 3D soundscaping software, the Noise Abatement Society and embracing ambient noise.

articleTitle: Password P R O 8 L 3 M $
abstract: John Mitchell recently had to set up a password. It had to be six to eight characters long, contain at least one upper case letter, one number and a special character. When he attempted to log-on he was asked for the second and sixth character of the password. At that stage he gave up and wrote it down.
Help with the direction of the Institute and make yourself heard by running for Council

articleTitle: The Value of Deconstructing Roles into Skills
abstract: The SFIA framework is not just for individuals; it has tangible organisational benefits too says Simon Roller FBCS CITP, Managing Director, Adaps Consulting.
The short answer to the question about whether entrepreneurs can be taught is ‘yes’. However, there are some important caveats, as Rob Wirszycz FBCS explains.
John McGlinchey, VP Europe and Middle East, CompTIA, provides some advice to trainers interested in tapping into a relatively untapped market, namely students.
The Real Time Club was founded in 1967 and is the oldest active IT-focused dining club anywhere. BCS Past President Geoff McMullen FBCS CITP explains why you may want to be involved in it.

With the words telehealth, telecare and telemedicine being bandied about so much these days it was perhaps apt that Dr Nicholas Robinson, Associate Clinical Director, Long-Term Conditions and Telehealth, NHS Direct, gave a talk about telehealth to the BCS Health (Northern) Group. Tom Sharpe MBCS reports.
Dr Justin Whatling, Vice Chair of BCS Health Strategy and Policy, explains the work BCS are engaged in to create clinical informatics leaders of the future.
Jo Twist is Chief Executive of UKIE (UK Interactive Entertainment) association. She spoke to Henry Tucker MBCS about what UKIE does, the UK games industry, innovation and helping small businesses.
The human can be both the weakest link and the strongest tool in building and protecting your organisation, says Gareth Niblett, Chair of BCS ISSG.

At the judging day for the UK IT Industry Awards, Henry Tucker MBCS spoke to some of the finalists in the business IT innovation category about the best pieces of careers advice they've been given and passed on to younger colleagues.
There is a lot more to online activistists, such as Anonymous, than the mainstream media would have us believe, says Gareth Niblett, Chair of BCS ISSG.
Dr Mark Samuels draws on CIO Connect research findings to show how CIOs must use consumerisation as an opportunity to redefine IT leadership.
When it comes to getting people to think about security, WendyGoucher MBCS, of Idrach, suggests appealing to their selfish side.

You are a highly trained and motivated security expert who seems to spend more time managing staff and doing paperwork than actual security work. You want to do more, but don't know what to do? Well you could serve your country according to one BCS member.

We have observed groups arrive on the hacking scene and one very notable representation is the now infamous Anonymous. John Walker FBCS CITP asks: who are they, what is there objective and what are the implications for the future?

Dr Julie Greensmith is part of the Intelligent Modelling and Analysis Group in the School of Computer Science at the University of Nottingham. She spoke to Justin Richards about her background and her work involving rollercoasters.
BCS Blogger Andrea Simmons MBCS looks at the impact of being wrong - in this context on the mechanisms for providing board-level assurance of relevant processes (controls) being reviewed.

At the BCS IT Awards judging day the shortlisted CIO of the year candidates gave invaluable insight into their careers and gave tips and hints of use to any IT professional. Justin Richards MBCS interviewed them.

The growth of the internet has transformed our everyday lives and today around eight per cent of the UK's GDP is generated by the internet. With this figure set to grow, making it larger than the utilities or agriculture sectors, the internet boom is predicted to create 365,000 jobs over the next five years according to the Office of Cyber Security & Information Assurance.
Gareth Niblett, Chairman of the BCS Information Security Specialist Group, takes a look at upcoming threats and countermeasures.

articleTitle: Software Quality and Testing as a Career
abstract: Steve Dennis, SQS Director, Training & Conferences Division, talks about the testing market, related job opportunities, the skills needed by testers and what the future holds for software quality assurance and testing training.
Following the recent launch of the PlayStation Vita, Sony's new portable gaming system, Henry Tucker MBCS tries his hand at some mobile gaming.
Dave Birch of Consult Hyperion takes some inspiration from TV science fiction to explore the concept of a psychic ID and see if modern technology can help bring his futuristic vision to reality.

Gerry Pennell CIO and Chris Payne, Head of Technology Operations Awareness, from LOCOG explain how their team designed and implemented all the technology that helped stage the London 2012 Olympic Games.
The BCS/RSI Annual Lecture for 2012 was entitled ‘Intelligence and Security in the Cyber Age’ and was given by Sir David Pepper KCMG, former Director of GCHQ. Brian Runciman MBCS attended.

Anti-virus (AV) software has played a critical role in the IT security industry for so long that it feels like it's an integral part of our computing systems. Over the years we have witnessed some extraordinary software development where hackers and AV vendors have played a spectacular game of cat and mouse as each tries to outwit the other says Ian McGowan MBCS.

The government has just published its new Information Strategy for England's National Health Service in the face of a certain amount of scepticism from various medical bodies. With this in mind Professor Stephen Kay FBCS, the BCS Health Informatics Standards representative, adds his own thoughts to the debate.

Vulnerable users equipped with corporate mobile devices - security time-bomb, or manageable situation? This is the mobile device balancing act according to Dr Sean Duignan, FBCS from the Galway-Mayo Institute of Technology.
2012 marks the 100th anniversary of the birth of Alan Turing. To commemorate this event we asked leading figures in IT what they think of Turing's legacy to computing.
BCS recently held a Thought Leadership debate to look at the question: ‘Do you think that you will be able to be a UK citizen in 10 years time without access to digital broadband services?’

While many focus on scare stories or coming threats of external hackers and the risks to our society from cyber terrorists, Bill Buchanan FBCS would like to outline a threat that he has observed over the past few years: the lack of fundamental theory from some computer security graduates.
With all the GAME shops now standing empty, does this mean that the future of games will be downloads? Henry Tucker MBCS hopes not.

During his year as Deputy President of BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, Roger Marshall is keeping a blog to give an insight into some of the activities that go on amongst the members. In this post he discusses what he's seen in Coventry and West Yorkshire.
Nigel Fenwick and John Brand of Forrester say: Forget IT strategy – to survive CIOs need business technology strategy

A few months ago HMRC published a consultation that has the potential to dramatically affect the way companies and public sector bodies engage senior level freelancers, contractors and interim staff says Simon McVicker, PCG's Head of Public Affairs.
Ian Herbert, Deputy Chair, BCS HIF, provides just a taste of the sizeable BCS Healthcare Specialist Group report ‘Fair Shares for all.’
The Institute publishes new reports from analyst Forrester every month. Members have access to the full text, this is an overview of recent reports.
Former cabinet minister Michael Portillo is still making waves. He spoke to Jim Cassidy from PCG about freelancing.

articleTitle: Book of the Month IT Manager's Handbook (3rd ed)

abstract: New tool launched for members to contribute to the Institute's discussions and consultations.
Just before the launch of its latest game, Henry Tucker MBCS spoke to Peter Hofstede, from Spil Games, about the challenges of mobile game development.
BCS author Robert Rowlingson says we shouldn't blame home PC users for poor security.

I have used the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the birth of Alan Turing to read more about him and his work. I confess that I've found him a far more interesting and vivid character than the ‘tragic genius’ motif would allow for, writes BCS Future Tech Blogger Chris Yapp FBCS.
IT professionalism and raising the profile of the industry are crucial for further success
Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Commercial Partner and TMT Sector Head, and Nadia Harto, Commercial Solicitor from Eversheds LLP, explain potential and proposed changes to EU data protection laws.
PCG's media advisor Jim Cassidy meets one of the UK's highest profile freelancers, Alistair Campbell.

Of course, BCS doesn't hold with gender stereotyping, but is there a role to play in encouraging women into technology businesses? A recent BCS Debate looked at some of the issues with Elizabeth Varley AMBCS, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Techhub and Maggie Berry MBCS Managing Director of Women in Technology. Brian Runciman MBCS hosted and reports.

articleTitle: Green Skills for the Green Economy
abstract: In the recently released ‘Skills for the Green Economy’ report from UK government, researchers identified that there are some £22 billion a year of potential savings to UK businesses that could be achieved by using raw materials, energy and water more efficiently. Brian Runciman MBCS reports on a BCS video debate that covered some of the issues.

Imagine the research processes of a scholar specialising in Jane Austen. What do their day to day methodologies entail? Close reading of Austen's texts, plus those of her contemporaries? Exhaustive analysis of parts of speech, the underlining of verbs and nouns, in her various books? Travelling to archives through-out the world to get access to Austen's correspondence and manuscripts? Keeping up with the various literature published on the topic? Melisssa Terras MBCS introduces digital humanities.

Over the past 40 years a service has developed from almost nothing to a £100Bn/annum worldwide business which we depend on in our daily lives and yet it is largely unknown. Paul Welsh MBCS CITP sheds light on intelligent transportation systems (ITS) and its many forms, used to run the services that keep the transport networks running smoothly as well as make life easier for drivers in their own vehicles.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Technology Partner and Head of TMT Sector, and Gillian Watkins, Senior Associate Solicitor, Human Resources Practice Group, of Eversheds LLP, take a look at some interesting cases around employees' use of social media as well as touching upon how to seek to un-blur the lines for employees between social and work time.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Commercial Partner and TMT Sector Head, and Farhan Khalid, trainee Solicitor, of Eversheds LLP, discuss recent hacking cases, the impact they have on organisations, and how they provide a stark reminder to us of the need to comply with our legal obligations.

Following the launch of the low cost Raspberry Pi, there has been significant discussion on how schools are failing students in provision of IT education. This article examines the challenges faced by Hayley Mitchell, a recent entrant into the IT industry, and some of the difficulties experienced by Sebastien Lahtinen, co-founder of thinkbroadband.com, in finding suitable candidates for the role in his organisation.

Despite the increasing adoption of open source software by heath care providers, it's becoming apparent that open source can never be seen as a ‘one shoe fits all’ policy and the decision to go down such a route must be carefully considered, weighing up each set of circumstances before taking the plunge. With this in mind Charles Mayes, Managing Director, DAV Management, weighs up some of the pros and cons that organisations, including health trusts, might face when considering this option.

Will there be a ‘hollowing out’ of UK IT staff as offshoring continues? Will specialisms be lost and does the UK needs tochange its attitude in the era of ‘follow the sun’ working? This article reports on a video debate covering these issues,and it also touches on our approach to specifying skill levels in tendering and a discussion of what the Institute's role should be.Participating were Elizabeth Sparrow, BCS past-President; John Milner, a freelance consultant previously of Cambridge University; Karim Hyatt an interim CIO involved in software products; and Gary Nuttall, a business intelligence expert. Brian Runciman MBCS hosted and reports.

Charlotte Walker-Osborn, Partner and Head of TMT Sector, Eversheds LLP and John McGrath, Principal Associate, Eversheds LLP, discuss some of the ways in which your business can utilise insurance to protect against cyber risks.

Skills shortages have become the bane of the IT industry. Many lay the blame with an education system which isn't doing enough to ingrain basic skills in young students or open them up to the opportunities of a career in IT. But while many focus on the problem of encouraging new entrants to the industry, employers are risking falling foul of a growing dissatisfaction among existing employees with the career development opportunities they are being offered. John Morris, Chief Executive of JAM, asks: is a lack of training holding back the UK software and electronics industry?

A survey by Version One found that 55 per cent of respondents claim agile methods have been successful in 90-100 per cent of cases. Critics say that agile methods don't scale properly. There's a middle ground as well, as exemplified by a 2008 Software Engineering Institute's technical report, which talked about the Capability Maturity Model and agile methods working together. Brian Runciman MBCS discussed the issues with Siamak Sham, Director of Radtac, Dale Titcombe from BCS, who runs a team of agile practitioners, and Stuart Reid, Chief Technical Officer of TSG. This report is an excerpt.

HC2012, this year's BCS Health Informatics Congress, took place at the Business Design Centre in London for the first time. However, change of venue aside, it was business as usual with a number of important and influential speakers on hand to lead on a variety of, at times, controversial topics.Matthew Swindells, Chair, BCS Health, reports on the opening plenary that asked the sticky question: are IT staff at the frontline of healthcare change?

BCS recently held a roundtable debate to discuss the security implications of the ‘bring your own device’ approach (BYOD). The debate was chaired by Brian Runciman MBCS with Louise Bennett FBCS CITP, Chair of the BCS Security Community of Expertise and Henry Tucker MBCS, Editor-in-Chief of ITNOW.

Ambient assisted living is attracting global interest especially within the chronic health and social care sectors. With this in mind Juan Carlos Augusto, School of Computing and Mathematics, University of Ulster at Jordanstown, explains the history of AAL and looks at its future applications.

articleTitle: User Adoption of Enterprise Resource Planning Systems
abstract: ERP systems require a substantial change programme; they are much more complex and far-reaching in terms of implementation and use, significantly changing the way in which people work. With this in mind IT training consultancy, Optimum Technology Transfer, recently conducted a survey amongst key personnel who are responsible for maintaining and upgrading ERP systems within end-using organisations. Samantha Markham and James Webb report on the challenges the survey revealed.

Step aside Deep Blue, Dr Dave Watson FBCS, IBM Director of Emerging Technology, discusses ‘Watson’ – a question and answer system that shows the future of unstructured data analytics, natural language processing and the design of workload optimised systems. The massively parallel processing system with an eight-core processor design that has a combined total of 16 terabytes of memory and can operate at over 80 teraflops (trillions of operations per second) could be set to change the world of health.

Some think that entrepreneurial skills are largely innate, others that they can be taught and of course there's a middle line. In a recent poll on the BCS website around 60 per cent thought that entrepreneurial skills could be taught. The issues were discussed by Christopher Thomas, Director at Sports Fusion; Timothy Barnes, Director of UCL Advances and Emma Jones from Start-up Britain, Founder of Enterprise Nation, Brian Runciman MBCS hosted and reports.

articleTitle: SFIA in Education and Workplace Learning
abstract: As this issue of ITNOW goes to print, the BCS Learning and Development Specialist Group will be celebrating its fifth anniversary and it has certainly been a year to remember. With this in mind Jooli Atkins FBCS, Group Chair, BCS L & D SG and Paul Jagger FBCS, IBM Certified Consulting Learning Specialist, report on one of the most important events of the group's fifth year; namely its first conference.

articleTitle: BBC Micro Past, Present and Future?
abstract: It's been just over 30 years since the BBC Microcomputer was launched by Acorn Computers in the United Kingdom, an event that inspired a generation of school children to learn about computers and programming at home and in schools. No surprise then that the recent Royal Society report (1) looking into the provision of computer science teaching and assessment in schools opens with mention of the BBC Micro. With the 30th anniversary of the BBC Micro in mind, IBM Certified Consulting Learning Specialist, Paul Jagger FBCS, reflects upon the BBC Micro - past, present and future.

Coaching and mentoring are widely used terms. Organisations look to coaching and mentoring for a number of reasons, but the bottom line is focused on what the actual business value is. Can we see increased productivity and profitability if we invest the time and money in either programme? The answer to this is ‘yes’ if the right steps are taken at implementation. Jooli Atkins, FBCS, Managing Director of Matrix FortyTwo and Doug Lawrence, founder of TalentC, shed some light on those steps.

A new video on information assurance featuring Baroness Neville-Jones, the Prime Minister's Special Representative on Cyber Security for Business, Chris Ensor, Head of Profession for IA at CESG, and Mike Westmacott, Security Consultant at IRM PLC, has been produced as BCS pilots an information assurance (IA) certification scheme with CESG, the information assurance arm of the Government Communications Headquarters (GCHQ) and the UK's National Technical Authority for Information Assurance.

A Canadian website for office rentals recently compared being an entrepreneur to walking a tightrope over Niagara Falls. The good news is that there is help. BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT is getting its feet wet in this arena with the launch of its new BCS Entrepreneurs Specialist Group and plenty of interesting resources. Brian Runciman MBCS takes an overview of entrepreneurialism.

articleTitle: Lessons from Janus? Repositioning Retained it at the Front of the Firm
abstract: CSC's Leading Edge Forum has been conducting next practice research for ambitious CIOs and executive teams at the intersection of business, IT and management for over 30 years. One of its recent reports focuses on the future of enterprise IT. ‘The role of the CIO today is to virtualise, consumerise and repurpose enterprise IT,’ says Richard Davies, VP and MD at the Leading Edge Forum.
